newsitem.title: UK: Malaysia's Mahathir says no plans to step down.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir says no plans to step down.

text.p: LONDON, May 20 (Reuter) Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Tuesday he had no plans to step down but, being mortal, could not go on for ever.
Mahathir, visiting London at the start of a two-month sabbatical, was asked at a news conference if he was planning to hand over power to Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
"No, it is not true that I am preparing to hand over, but the fact remains that at some stage or another I have to stop becoming the prime minister," he replied.
"There is no way a person could stay on even after he is dead."

Mahathir, 71, has appointed Anwar as acting prime minister in his absence -- the first time in his 16 years in power that he has named an acting premier. The move prompted speculation that he may be preparing to step down for health reasons.

"On major issues, I still think I should consult him...but I wouldn't want to bother him with details because he has given me full trust and confidence," Anwar told reporters in Manila where he was attending a conference.
"I want him to rest. I want him to concentrate on other things. I want him to think and read and write and then come back re-energised," Anwar said.
Mahathir was visiting London to promote investment in the information technology business on the Multimedia Super Corridor, a high technology zone being created near Kuala Lumpur.
The prime minister will visit several countries including Poland, Hungary and Switzerland as part of his work and rest break.
